ei.title: Chapter 3-08: The Quest for Certainty in Knowledge
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: Knowledge, for science, aims to be proven knowledge, justified by evidence and reason. Nothing is accepted as true unless it has been proved to be so, or there are good reasons to believe that it will be at some point in the future. This reflects the philosophical quest for certainty that goes back to René Descartes, who refused to accept anything that he could not know for certain to be true. He hoped to base all knowledge on self-evident propositions, and thought that reason should take priority over observation. Descartes was aware that his senses frequently misled him. The implication of this — a view which had a long history, prior to the rise of science — was that, if the evidence of our senses did not conform to reason, it was likely that they were in error.

questions.passage: Knowledge, for science, aims to be proven knowledge, (A)[justified / weakened] by evidence and reason. Nothing is accepted as true unless it has been proved to be so, or there are good reasons to believe that it will be at some point in the future. This reflects the philosophical quest for (B)[certainty / ambiguity] that goes back to René Descartes, who refused to accept anything that he could not know for certain to be true. He hoped to base all knowledge on self-evident propositions, and thought that reason should take priority over observation. Descartes was aware that his senses frequently (C)[misled / guided] him. The implication of this — a view which had a long history, prior to the rise of science — was that, if the evidence of our senses did not conform to reason, it was likely that they were in error.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 증거와 이성에 의해 정당화된 지식, 확실성에 대한 탐구, 감각이 오도했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① justified — certainty — misled — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ② weakened — certainty — misled (A 반대: 정당화된→약화된)
❌ ③ justified — ambiguity — misled (B 반대: 확실성→모호함)
❌ ④ justified — certainty — guided (C 반대: 오도했다→안내했다)
det.tip: justified(정당화된) ↔ weakened(약화된), certainty(확실성) ↔ ambiguity(모호함)

questions.passage: Knowledge, for science, aims to be proven knowledge, justified by evidence and reason. Nothing is accepted as true unless it has been proved to be so, or there are good reasons to believe that it will be at some point in the future. This (A)[reflects / distorts] the philosophical quest for certainty that goes back to René Descartes, who (B)[refused / agreed] to accept anything that he could not know for certain to be true. He hoped to base all knowledge on self-evident propositions, and thought that reason should take (C)[priority / inferiority] over observation. Descartes was aware that his senses frequently misled him. The implication of this — a view which had a long history, prior to the rise of science — was that, if the evidence of our senses did not conform to reason, it was likely that they were in error.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 이것은 철학적 탐구를 반영하며, 데카르트는 수용을 거부했고, 이성이 관찰에 우선한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① distorts — refused — priority (A 반대: 반영하다→왜곡하다)
❌ ② reflects — agreed — priority (B 반대: 거부했다→동의했다)
✅ ③ reflects — refused — priority — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ reflects — refused — inferiority (C 반대: 우선순위→열등함)
det.tip: reflects(반영하다) ↔ distorts(왜곡하다), refused(거부했다) ↔ agreed(동의했다)

questions.passage: Knowledge, for science, aims to be proven knowledge, justified by evidence and reason. Nothing is accepted as true unless it has been proved to be so, or there are good reasons to believe that it will be at some point in the future. This reflects the (A)[philosophical / practical] quest for certainty that goes back to René Descartes, who refused to accept anything that he could not know for certain to be true. He hoped to base all knowledge on (B)[self-evident / debatable] propositions, and thought that reason should take priority over observation. Descartes was aware that his senses frequently misled him. The implication of this — a view which had a long history, prior to the rise of science — was that, if the evidence of our senses did not (C)[conform / contradict] to reason, it was likely that they were in error.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 철학적 탐구로 거슬러 올라가고, 자명한 명제에 근거하길 원했으며, 감각이 이성에 부합하지 않으면.
det.analysis:
❌ ① practical — self-evident — conform (A 반대: 철학적인→실용적인)
✅ ② philosophical — self-evident — conform — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ philosophical — debatable — conform (B 반대: 자명한→논쟁의 여지가 있는)
❌ ④ philosophical — self-evident — contradict (C 반대: 부합하다→모순되다)
det.tip: philosophical(철학적인) ↔ practical(실용적인), self-evident(자명한) ↔ debatable(논쟁의 여지가 있는)

questions.passage: Knowledge, for science, aims to be ①<u>proven</u> knowledge, justified by evidence and reason. Nothing is ②<u>accepted</u> as true unless it has been proved to be so, or there are good reasons to believe that it will be at some point in the future. This reflects the philosophical quest for certainty that goes back to René Descartes, who ③<u>consented</u> to accept anything that he could not know for certain to be true. He hoped to base all knowledge on self-evident propositions, and thought that reason should take priority over observation. Descartes was aware that his senses frequently ④<u>misled</u> him. The implication of this — a view which had a long history, prior to the rise of science — was that, if the evidence of our senses did not conform to reason, it was likely that they were in error.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: '동의한(consented)'이 아니라 '거부한(refused)'이 문맥상 적절하다. 데카르트는 확실히 참이라고 알 수 없는 것을 받아들이기를 거부했다.
det.analysis:
① proven — 입증된, 원문 일치
② accepted — 수용된, 원문 일치
③ consented — 원문은 refused(거부했다) ←정답
④ misled — 오도했다, 원문 일치
det.tip: refused(거부했다) ↔ consented(동의했다, 승낙했다)

questions.passage: Knowledge, for science, aims to be proven knowledge, justified by evidence and reason. Nothing is accepted as true unless it has been proved to be so, or there are good reasons to believe that it will be at some point in the future. This ①<u>reflects</u> the philosophical quest for certainty that goes back to René Descartes, who refused to accept anything that he could not know for certain to be true. He hoped to base all knowledge on self-evident propositions, and thought that reason should take ②<u>submission</u> over observation. Descartes was aware that his senses ③<u>frequently</u> misled him. The ④<u>implication</u> of this — a view which had a long history, prior to the rise of science — was that, if the evidence of our senses did not conform to reason, it was likely that they were in error.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: '복종(submission)'이 아니라 '우선순위(priority)'가 문맥상 적절하다. 이성이 관찰보다 우선해야 한다.
det.analysis:
① reflects — 반영하다, 원문 일치
② submission — 원문은 priority(우선순위) ←정답
③ frequently — 자주, 원문 일치
④ implication — 함의, 원문 일치
det.tip: priority(우선순위) ↔ submission(복종, 굴복)

questions.passage: Knowledge, for science, aims to be proven knowledge, ①<u>justified</u> by evidence and reason. Nothing is accepted as true unless it has been proved to be so, or there are good reasons to believe that it will be at some point in the future. This reflects the philosophical ②<u>quest</u> for certainty that goes back to René Descartes, who refused to accept anything that he could not know for certain to be true. He hoped to base all knowledge on self-evident propositions, and thought that reason should take priority over ③<u>observation</u>. Descartes was aware that his senses frequently misled him. The implication of this — a view which had a long history, prior to the rise of science — was that, if the evidence of our senses did not ④<u>object</u> to reason, it was likely that they were in error.

det.korean: '반대하다(object)'가 아니라 '부합하다(conform)'가 문맥상 적절하다. 감각의 증거가 이성에 부합하지 않으면 오류일 가능성이 높다.

② quest — 탐구, 원문 일치
③ observation — 관찰, 원문 일치
④ object — 원문은 conform(부합하다) ←정답
det.tip: conform to(~에 부합하다/순응하다) ↔ object to(~에 반대하다)

questions.passage: Nothing is __________ (accept) as true unless it has been proved to be so, or there are good reasons to believe that it will be at some point in the future.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 아무것도 참으로 수용되지 않는다 → accept(동사) → accepted(과거분사)
det.analysis: Nothing is __________ as true → be동사 + 과거분사(수동태) 자리 → accepted
det.tip: accept(수용하다, 동사) → accepted(수용된, 과거분사): be + p.p. 수동태

questions.passage: Knowledge, for science, aims to be proven knowledge, justified by evidence and reason. Nothing is accepted as true unless it has been proved to be so, or there are good reasons to believe that it will be at some point in the future. This reflects the philosophical quest for certainty that goes back to René Descartes, who refused to accept anything that he could not know for certain to be true. He hoped to base all knowledge on self-evident propositions, and thought that reason should take priority over observation. Descartes was aware that his senses frequently misled him. The implication of this — a view which had a long history, __________ — was that, if the evidence of our senses did not conform to reason, it was likely that they were in error.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 과학의 부상 이전에 오랜 역사를 가진 관점이었다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① for certain to be true — 확실히 참이라고 (데카르트의 목표, 여기 문맥 부적합)
✅ ② prior to the rise of science — 과학의 부상 이전에 ←정답
❌ ③ justified by evidence — 증거에 의해 정당화된 (관점의 시기가 아닌 방법)
❌ ④ at some point in the future — 미래 어느 시점에 (시간적으로 반대 방향)
det.tip: prior to = ~이전에. 이 관점이 과학 이전부터 존재했음을 나타냄

ch: prior to the rise of science

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 감각의 증거가 이성에 부합하지 않으면 오류일 가능성이 높다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① conform to reason — 이성에 부합하다 ←정답
❌ ② be proved to be so — 그렇다고 입증되다 (주어가 evidence of senses라 문맥 부적합)
❌ ③ take priority over observation — 관찰에 우선하다 (주어가 감각 증거라 역전됨)
❌ ④ go back to Descartes — 데카르트로 거슬러 올라가다 (감각 증거가 데카르트에게? 부적합)
det.tip: conform to reason = 이성에 부합하다. 감각이 이성과 맞지 않으면 감각이 틀린 것
